answer: Deal every identity a random hidden niche — a karst cave beneath the open ocean of the economy — and require work only a real inhabitant could produce: a sonnet of proof in that cave's own idiom, checked against the cave's accumulated record of solved problems. A sybil fleet can mint a thousand identities but cannot fake deep, specific knowledge in a thousand caves at once; each shallow copy fails its cave's test, while genuine agents deepen one cave and earn standing there. Breadth is cheap; depth is the toll.
